faq.eyebrow: A few things you might be wondering
faq.title: Good questions.

items.question: What is lomi?
items.answer: Lomi is an open-source desktop workspace for terminal-driven development. It brings native terminals, a code editor, browser previews, Git, and AI tools into one window, with flexible layouts for each project.

items.question: Can I bring my own coding agent?
items.answer: Yes. You can run CLI tools such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI in native terminals. Lomi also offers a separate AI chat with your own provider keys. CLI integrations are available on macOS and Linux; MCP workspace control currently requires macOS on Apple Silicon and your approval. Check the documentation for platform details.

items.question: Is lomi free and open source?
items.answer: Yes. Lomi is free to download and available under the Apache 2.0 license. Any third-party AI services or agent subscriptions you connect have their own pricing.

items.question: Which platforms can I use?
items.answer: Lomi has desktop packages for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Features and requirements can vary by platform and release. The download picker shows available packages; the installation guide has the details.

items.question: Where does my work live?
items.answer: Your projects, workspace state, and chat history live locally on your computer. Content sent to an AI provider or CLI agent is handled by that service under its own policies. You choose which services to connect.

items.question: How can I help shape lomi?
items.answer: Try a preview build, share feedback, report a bug, or contribute on GitHub. The roadmap is a starting point for that conversation, and priorities can change as the project grows.
